title: Asymmetric weight swap — canary debrief and mitigations
content:
Executive summary:

On 2024-05-09 at ~15:42 UTC we observed a degradation in canary model health for the staging canary cohort (canary-region-us-west-2). Symptoms included a sharp rise in token-decode mismatch errors, perplexity drift on a fixed probe set, and intermittent OOMs reported by several GPUs running the new model bundle. The canary error budget was breached within 18 minutes of rollout start.

This incident was caused by an asymmetric weight shard application during a staged rollout: a subset of canary hosts received the new model weight shards (v2.1) while others were still serving the previous shards (v2.0) due to an out-of-order apply job combined with a missing cross-check on manifest signatures. The mismatch manifested as inconsistent KV cache expectations and subtle tokenizer decoding differences (token ID mapping drift) for long contexts.

Impact and scope:
- Affected cohort: staging canary (12 hosts). Production was not impacted; traffic routing prevented promotion.
- Observable effects: token-decode mismatch rate spiked from ~0.02% baseline to 6.4% at peak; probe perplexity increased by ~28%; transient OOMs on 3/12 canary hosts causing request drops and reconnect storms.
- Time to mitigate (pause + rollback): 22 minutes from first alert to stable baseline on staging.

Detection timeline (UTC):
- 15:38 — Canary rollout job for model v2.1 initiated (rolling apply shards across 12 hosts, batch size=3).
- 15:42 — First alert: canary-decode-mismatch rate crosses 1% threshold (Grafana alert). Pager to oncall SRE.
- 15:44 — Oncall begins investigation. Noted config_apply jobs finishing with exit code 0 but inconsistent weight checksums across hosts.
- 15:47 — Two hosts report OOMs; autoscaler attempts restart, restarts fail with load-time assertion in kernel selection.
- 15:50 — Canaries show divergent token-id histograms on probe request path. Decision made to pause rollout and stop further apply jobs.
- 15:56 — Coordinated rollback to v2.0 manifest issued to all 12 canary hosts; checksum-verified load completed by 16:00.
- 16:10 — System metrics returned to baseline, canary probe metrics stable by 16:12. Post-rollback health checks passed.

Immediate remediation steps executed:
1) Paused rollout via orchestrator (rollout controller -> pause).
2) Disabled parallel apply workers to prevent further out-of-order shard application.
3) Issued rollback manifest (v2.0 signed manifest) and enforced checksum validation on load.
4) Recovered affected hosts via full restart and validated KV cache warmup using known probe sequence.
5) Raised incident channel and documented initial findings for engineering and product.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis validated by artifact traces):
- Primary cause: orchestration race in the weight-apply subsystem. The apply job scheduler allowed overlapping apply windows when hosts reported slow disk IO; that caused shards to be applied in different sequences and left some hosts with mixed-generation contiguous shards (partial v2 + partial v1).
- Contributing cause: unsigned transient manifest used during fast rollout path. The rollout controller assumed atomic replace semantics, but the apply procedure is actually two-phase (fetch -> write -> activate) and lacked a final atomic activation barrier across shards.
- Resulting failure mode: asymmetric binary layout caused the runtime kernel selector to choose incompatible execution paths for KV cache offsets and embedding projection alignment. This produced memory indexing anomalies culminating in OOMs on certain GPUs and token id mapping drift for long contexts.
- Why the canary alerts triggered late: our usual canary smoke (latency, error-rate) did not include deterministic token-id/decoding probes; we only had a high-level perplexity probe which lags these deeper decode mismatches.

Logs and artifacts examined (representative):
- Orchestrator logs: rollout-controller:apply: host-03 apply completed 15:40:12 checksum=abc123, host-05 apply completed 15:40:14 checksum=def456 (mismatched), host-03 activate started before host-05 finished write.
- Host kernel logs: runtime:kv-cache: expected-kv-offset=0x7f4a, observed 0x7f4b -> index out-of-range warnings preceding OOM.
- Probe traces: fixed-probe "decode-test-7" token-id histogram divergence (sha1 of token-id-seq): v1_hosts=5d6f... vs v2_partial_hosts=9b2c...

Short-term action items completed during incident:
- Rollback to v2.0 across all canaries and verify stable baseline (done).
- Turn off parallel shard apply workers (temporary configuration flag) to avoid additional asymmetric applies (done).
- Increase verbosity for weight apply and activation events (done).

Post-incident remediation (owner and ETA):
1) Enforce signed manifests + manifest activation handshake (owner: Maya Lin, ETA: 2024-05-20).
2) Add per-host pre-activation checksum compare step that aborts activation if any shard checksum differs from manifest (owner: Ethan Park, ETA: 2024-05-16).
3) Update rollout controller to use per-rollout global lock for activation phase or transactional activation barrier (owner: Carlos Ortega, ETA: 2024-05-23).
4) Implement deterministic decode-canary probe run as part of canary smoke (3 probe sequences that validate token ID sequence and hash post-load) (owner: Priya Menon, ETA: 2024-05-14).
5) CI: add integration test that performs staggered shard apply across fake hosts and asserts no partial-activation state can be observed (owner: Zoe Chen, ETA: 2024-06-01).
6) Dashboarding: add "token-decode-mismatch" metric and alert with a lower threshold for canary cohorts (owner: eng-observability, ETA: 2024-05-12).

Runbook updates required (short checklist):
- New section: "Detecting asymmetric weight application" with commands to fetch per-host manifests, checksums, and activation timestamps (include sample curl/gcloud commands).
- Add explicit rollback playbook when checksum mismatch + decode divergence observed.
- Include guidance to avoid immediate retry/apply cycles; prefer abort/inspect.
- Add troubleshooting snippet: how to extract token-id histogram from recent traces and compare sha1 checksums against expected probe hashes.

Lessons learned and follow-ups:
- Even in a staged rollout, atomic activation semantics (all-or-nothing) for model activation are essential; partial binary mixes are dangerous for any system with stateful KV cache and position-dependent kernels.
- Smoke tests must include deterministic decoding probes, not only high-level perplexity or token loss metrics. A small deterministic probe is low-cost and highly effective.
- Alert thresholds: we will add a low-threshold decode-mismatch alert specifically for canary cohorts to catch these classes of regressions earlier.
- Operational play: prefer single-threaded applies or coordinated activation barrier for slow IO hosts rather than aggressive parallelism.

Appendix: quick commands used during incident:
- rollout-controller pause: POST /api/rollouts/<id>/pause
- fetch per-host checksum: curl -s http://host-05.internal:7000/weights/manifest | jq .checksums
- probe-run post-load: python tools/run_probe.py --model-endpoint host-03:7000 --probe decode-test-7 --output /tmp/probe-host-03.json

Open questions (to be resolved in postmortem meeting):
- Should the rollout orchestrator enforce a "write->verify->quiesce->activate" flow by default? (pro: safety, con: slower deploys).
- For large-model shards with long load times, can we introduce a staggered activation strategy that prefers atomic activation across groups rather than individual hosts to reduce partial-state windows?

Next steps: schedule a 60-minute post-incident review with Eng SRE, Serving Runtime, and Orchestration owners (Maya, Carlos, Ethan, Zoe) to finalize root cause, PR list, and confirm ETA commitments. Suggested window: 2024-05-11 16:00 UTC.

Document owner contact: priya.m@redwood.ai
